tool_input.new_string:
**A ninth, found 2026-09-22 on a later OPES-62 run:** the `tests` station was dispatched
with no execution tool at all — only Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep — while its own prompt
requires it to "run the tests yourself and confirm they fail" and to check the pre-existing
suite still passes. The station can only verify statically, so a test file that does not
compile reaches the freeze unnoticed. That is the same hole defect #4 came through.

**The full write-up with evidence** was handed to the maintainer as a file on 2026-09-22.

result:
Tests are written. One thing I have to flag plainly: **I could not run them.**

## What I wrote

`src/features/home/HomeScreen.test.tsx` — the only file in the plan's `files.tests`. Nothing in `files.change` was touched.

Seven cases, one per criterion, each carrying its id in the test name and asserting the criterion's literal:

| AC | assertion | expected at freeze |
|---|---|---|
| AC-001 | `loadCardsByUser` called `1` after mount+focus | **green** |
| AC-002 | called `2` after a second focus | **red** |
| AC-003 | `queryAllByTestId('home-card')` has length `1` after refocus | **red** |
| AC-004 | called `1` when status flips to `connected` | **green** |
| AC-005 | called `1` when a saved token connects during mount | **green** |
| AC-006 | called `1` after pull-to-refresh | **green** |
| AC-007 | called `1` after a foreground sync | **green** |

Five green is what the ticket itself predicts: the bug is a *missing* re-render on a transition, not a wrong end state, so only AC-002 and AC-003 can go red against today's screen. I did not manufacture red for the other five — each has a control assertion (`loadTransactions` ran, the sync really fired with `{ silent: true }`) so a count of `1` means the screen declined to re-read, not that the trigger never landed.

## Deviations from the plan, and why

- **D-005** says the fake `useFocusEffect` is `useEffect(cb, [focusTick])`. I used `useEffect(cb, [cb, focusTick])`. The real hook re-subscribes on callback identity — that is exactly what D-002 quotes as the reason the callback must be memoised. With `cb` out of the deps, an un-memoised inline arrow is indistinguishable from a memoised one and AC-004/AC-005 assert nothing about it. The comment in the file records this.
- **Plan prose** says `render(...)` once into a shared element. I build a fresh element per render: handing `rerender` the same element object lets React bail out of the subtree on referential equality, and AC-002/AC-003/AC-004 would have read a stale tree.

## The verification I owe you and did not do

This session gave me no Bash or other execution tool — only read/write/search. So I never ran `npm test`, `tsc`, or the lint guard. I verified statically instead: every mocked path matches the screen's imports; `makeCard`, `ThemeProvider` and `RenderResult` all resolve; the test name and placement satisfy `testMatch` and the guard; the `var`-knob and requireActual patterns are copied from suites already passing in this repo. Two API facts I checked in `node_modules` rather than assumed — RNTL 14 has **no** `UNSAFE_getByType` (my first draft used it; it is gone), and React Native's jest `ScrollView` mock spreads props onto `RCTScrollView`, which is how `pullToRefresh` reaches `onRefresh`.

That last one is the weakest link: if the refresh handler is not reachable that way, AC-006 fails by `throw`, which is a wrong-reason red. It should be the first thing checked when the suite is actually executed.

Separately — the tests station being dispatched without an execution tool while its prompt requires it to run the suite is the same class of hole as gate defect #4. I tried to record it in the project memory on the aif defects and a hook rejected the write, so it is only here.
